steps.desc: A team claims their message workflow is “secure”. Audit it, then fix it hands-on in a live console.
steps.intro: Hi, I’m Hana, your senior analyst. A team swears their file sharing is “totally secure”. Nobody has checked. Let’s test it together.

steps.title: 3 things that make file sharing secure

tips.start: Quick primer first. Tap each card to flip it.
tips.done: You’ve got the basics. Time to investigate!

cards.title: Strong cipher
cards.back: Use modern authenticated encryption like AES-256-GCM. Old ciphers such as DES can be cracked.

cards.title: Separate key
cards.back: Never send the key with the file. Share it another way, so one leak can’t unlock everything.

cards.title: Limited access
cards.back: Links should reach named people only, and expire. “Anyone with the link” means anyone.

steps.title: Tap the 3 weak spots in this workflow

tips.start: Something here isn’t as secure as it looks…
tips.ready: Happy with your picks? Hit Check.
tips.good: Sharp eyes! Next, let’s actually fix it.
tips.bad: Close! Look at what turned orange.

good.title: Sharp eyes!
good.text: Weak cipher, key sent with the file and a public link. You caught all three.

bad.title: Not quite
bad.text: The weak spots were the encryption, the key sharing and the share link.

steps.title: Fix it in the console, then run the attack

settings.hint: How the recipient gets the key

settings.label: Link access
settings.hint: Who can open the share link

tips.start: This is their live config. Pick the setting you trust most in each row, then run the attack simulator.
tips.progress: Happy with every row? Run the attack and see what gets through.
tips.good: Every attack bounced off. Great work!
tips.bad: Something got through. Check what’s still orange.

good.title: Attack blocked!
good.text: Strong cipher, separate key, named recipients and a short expiry. Nothing got through.

bad.title: Breach!
bad.text: Attackers got in through the settings still marked orange. Use the strongest option in each row.

left.text: Key sent in the same chat

tips.start: Tap a problem, then the fix that solves it.
tips.progress: Keep pairing. Tap a pair again to undo it.
tips.ready: All paired up? Check your matches.
tips.good: Perfect match! You really get it.
tips.bad: Nearly. The orange pairs were mixed up.

good.title: Perfect match!
good.text: You know exactly how to fix each weak spot.

bad.title: Not quite
bad.text: DES → AES-256-GCM, key in the same chat → share it separately, public link → named people and an expiry date.

debrief.headline: Mission complete!
debrief.sub: You found the weak spots and locked the workflow down in the console.
